events.what: Banerjee proves Beilinson's conjecture unconditionally for certain K3 surfaces over the algebraic closure of Q admitting an involution with quotient P^2 branched along a sextic
events.credibility_reason: Single-author preprint on a hard Chow-group statement (Bloch-Beilinson type, over Q-bar); no expert uptake recorded; revised 2026-03-05 without the record saying what changed.

events.what: Broe gives a criterion for the Beilinson-Bloch conjecture over global function fields and deduces it for products of curves with powers of CM elliptic curves
Banerjee proves the Bloch-Beilinson conjecture for certain abelian surfaces over Q conditional on BSD for them
Peng makes conditional/partial progress on Beilinson-Bloch-Kato for polarized motives

judgement.doubts: Partial rests on unreviewed special cases of the Bloch-Beilinson/Beilinson-Bloch branch of the conjectural family; if the bullet is read narrowly as Beilinson's L-value/regulator conjectures only, these are variants and the status would be open. The two conditional results (reductions to BSD or other unproven hypotheses) cannot set status. Broe is the more solid of the two surviving cases; both are confirmed, no AI, so the codes don't change.

corrections.why: other: Peng's arXiv:2509.18615 is described in the summary as 'conditional/partial progress', i.e. a reduction to unproven conditions (scope none), so it cannot support the partial status. Banerjee's K3 and Broe's function-field cases are the surviving case settlements.

F1/F2: kept. The unconditional K3 case (arXiv:2502.09380) and the function-field case (arXiv:2505.00696) are unreviewed case settlements, so the tier is partial, not claimed. Doubt: the record's competing_reading points out they concern the Bloch-Beilinson/Beilinson-Bloch branch rather than the L-value/regulator conjectures. Also the K3 claim is single-author and nobody has taken it up.
